title: Acknowledgement & self-verify kit for transient embedding divergence
content:
Purpose:

This note is a customer-facing draft to acknowledge the transient embedding divergence incident that affected a subset of hosted API requests on 2027-11-08 UTC. It provides a short status update suitable for the status page, a concise postmortem summary for customers, and a reproducible self-verification checklist customers can run to confirm that their data and inference results are consistent.

TL;DR (to appear on status page):
- Incident: transient embedding divergence causing small subsets of embedding requests to differ from expected fingerprints for ~27 minutes in region eu-west-1.
- Impact: roughly 0.6% of embedding requests received a divergent vector variant. No data loss; text generation and chat endpoints were not affected.
- Current status: mitigated and fixed. All affected requests have been reconciled; customers can self-verify using the steps below.

Suggested short status page copy (100–200 chars):
We experienced brief embedding inconsistencies in eu-west-1 on 2027-11-08 UTC. Root cause identified and fixed; self-verify kit available. No data loss.

Customer-facing postmortem summary (concise):
What happened:
On 2027-11-08 at ~10:04 UTC, a configuration roll that altered a kernel-selection heuristic caused an unexpected quantization path for a small percentage of embedding requests in eu-west-1. The change produced embeddings with small numeric deviations (mean cosine drift ~0.0027) and, for a narrow subset of inputs (customer-provided prompt patterns that hit a rare codepath), produced a divergent variant.

Scope and impact:
- Affected surface: embeddings endpoint only, region eu-west-1.
- Customer impact: 0.6% of embedding requests during the window had variant outputs that might change nearest-neighbor lookup results for edge cases (very tight similarity thresholds).
- No textual generation/chat responses were impacted; no customer data was deleted or modified.

Root cause (summary):
During a routine runtime optimization deployment, an updated kernel selection rule incorrectly preferred a mixed-precision quantized execution path for certain sequence-lengths and model variants. The runtime fallback that verifies fingerprints did not trigger due to a timing race between the rollout and a cache-priming event.

Immediate remediation taken:
1) We rolled back the kernel-selection change at 10:31 UTC.
2) We enabled an emergency guard that forces the pre-change kernel selection for all embedding models in eu-west-1 at 10:33 UTC.
3) We ran a reconciliation job to detect and mark potentially divergent responses and re-ran inference for affected tenant queues where safe at 11:02–11:42 UTC.

Current status (what customers should know):
- The platform is operating normally.
- We completed a reconciliation pass for all requests during the window and retracted any divergent vectors from the embeddings cache used for read-your-writes scenarios.
- If you use strict similarity thresholds (<0.8) in production, please run the self-verify steps below; if you prefer, request an evidence package from your account rep and we will run the verification on your behalf.

Self-verify checklist (repro steps for customers):
Note: these steps are safe read-only checks. They will not modify data. Replace placeholders with your values.
1) Identify a sample of queries submitted between 2027-11-08T10:04:00Z and 2027-11-08T10:31:00Z. If you do not log timestamps, choose a random sample of 50 recent embedding calls and include the request_id returned by the API.

2) Retrieve stored embeddings (if you persist them) and compute the cosine similarity to a re-generated embedding:
- Curl example to re-create embedding:
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-3", "input": "<<YOUR_TEXT>>"}' | jq '.data[0].embedding'

- Locally compute cosine similarity to your persisted vector (python snippet):
  from numpy import dot, linalg
  import json
  a = json.loads(persisted_vector_json)
  b = json.loads(regenerated_vector_json)
  cos = dot(a,b)/(linalg.norm(a)*linalg.norm(b))
  print(cos)

3) Divergence thresholds and interpretation:
- Expected normal numeric jitter: cosine >= 0.998.
- Minor divergence: 0.990 <= cosine < 0.998 — unlikely to materially change most similarity results.
- Edge divergence: cosine < 0.990 — may change nearest-neighbor ordering in tight-threshold systems (this is the bucket we targeted for reconciliation).

4) If you find vectors with cosine < 0.990 and you want Redwood to validate and re-run inference for your tenant, open a ticket with the subject: "Embedding divergence review — tenant <TENANT_ID>" and include up to 200 sample request_ids (or persisted vectors). We will prioritize verification and, if needed, perform a replay and reconciliation on your behalf.

Evidence and artifact package (what we can provide on request):
- Per-tenant list of request_ids during the window, along with our internal divergence score and reconciliation action (noop / replayed / customer consent required).
- Hash fingerprints of pre- and post-replay vectors (SHA256 of serialized float32 array) for independent verification.

Compensation and remediation options (customer choices):
- For customers with production contracts: service credit equivalent to 1 day's average embed usage for tenants where divergence materially changed results (post-verification).
- Option for Redwood to run a targeted replay for affected tenants (requires customer approval) and deliver an evidence bundle.

FAQ (short):
Q: Did Redwood change customer data?
A: No. No persisted customer data was altered or deleted. All reconciliation steps were read-only or replayed under customer-approved flows.

Q: Could this affect downstream models (retrieval-augmented generation)?
A: Potentially only if your RAG pipeline depends on very tight similarity thresholds for retrieval. Most systems with wider thresholds (>0.85) will not see meaningful differences.

Q: How can I avoid this class of issue in the future?
A: We now have a runbook that includes a traffic-mirroring validation step and stronger runtime fingerprint assertions during kernel-selection changes. If you require stricter determinism, consider: pinning to a specific model variant, enabling embedding version pinning in the Dedicated or Private product, or adding an internal checksum middleware.

Internal notes for CS reps:
- If a customer requests evidence, route to engineering incident team with tag INC-4821 and include tenant id + up to 200 sample request ids.
- For top-tier customers, pre-approve replay runs; for others, require explicit written consent before re-running inference at scale.

Next steps (engineering commitments):
- Deploy a guard that will compare runtime fingerprint before completing kernel selection (owner: serving-runtime; ETA: 2027-11-16).
- Add a multi-tenant reconciliation tool accessible to CS with audit logs (owner: solutions-engineering; ETA: 2027-11-24).
- Postmortem doc: full technical write-up published to Confluence and linked on the public status page (owner: incident-review; ETA: 2027-11-18).

Contact:
If you want Redwood to run verification or request an evidence package, open a ticket at https://redwood.atlassian.net/secure/CreateIssue!default.jspa (project: CSUPPORT) or email cs-support@redwood.ai with subject line: "Embedding divergence review — <TENANT_ID>".

Draft status and approvals needed:
- Draft prepared by: Maya Chen (CS).
- Technical verification by: Jordan Lee (serving-runtime) pending — expected 2027-11-11.
- Legal/comms sign-off required for public postmortem snippet before status page publish.

Notes to reviewers (internal):
- Keep public status page copy concise and non-technical. Use the postmortem summary for customer emails.
- This draft intentionally includes reproducible checks so customers can independently verify; avoid exposing low-level internal logs in the public artifact.

End of draft.
